rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to retain early compounds while promoting elution of all 10 within the acquisition window. The retention and resolution pattern will guide subsequent gradient and temperature adjustments.

Use an intermediate temperature to seek favorable selectivity between the two observed crowded patterns. A modestly shallower gradient should add resolution while keeping the last peak near the zero-time-penalty region.
Increase temperature by 5 °C to try to separate the remaining close pair while preserving the other resolution margins. Keeping the gradient unchanged should retain the zero time penalty.

Test a slightly higher starting organic fraction as a distinct nearby alternative to the maximum-scoring method. This may shorten retention while shifting selectivity in the two least-resolved pairs.
